title: Kmen's own style across groups
summary: Kmen adapts his playing to modern, swing or traditional groups.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: playing. Well, to get down to a specific personal case, do you try to play one style yourself or do you vary your style a lot depending on who you're playing with?

Because I've played so long, I don't even try to vary my style. I'm forced to vary my style. I've tried to keep up all these years and if I'm playing with a modern group, I play modern. But if I'm playing with a Dixie group, say, a traditional group, I play as best I can. It certainly has that kind of overall feeling, traditional. Now, there's some overlapping but I couldn't play a modern line against a traditional rhythm section or play a traditional line against a modern rhythm section. And if it's a swing group, I'll play more or less in that style. And, of course, my ideal is to combine the best of all of them if I can, ultimately. ... ... ... ... ... ...
